chunks: Hadith 2787 — Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abū Ayyūb Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUthmān al-Khazzāz, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in Makkah when a man entered upon him and said: “May Allah set you aright. We have with us a menstruating woman, and she has not performed Tawāf al-Nisāʾ, and the camel driver refuses to remain for her.”
He said: Then he lowered his head while saying: “She is not able to stay behind her companions, and her camel driver will not remain for her.”
Then he raised his head toward him and said: “She may proceed, for her hajj has been completed.”

key_terms.الْجَمَّالُ: the camel driver or caravan handler responsible for transport
key_terms.تَتَخَلَّفَ: to remain behind or stay back from the group
key_terms.تَمْضِي: she may go on or depart
key_terms.حَائِضًا: a menstruating woman, whose ritual state affects certain hajj rites
key_terms.حَجُّهَا: her hajj, meaning her pilgrimage rites as a whole
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: the Tawaf al-Nisa, the circumambulation associated with the lawfulness of marital relations after hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a menstruating woman cannot perform Tawāf al-Nisāʾ before leaving with her caravan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a menstruating woman who was unable to perform Tawāf al-Nisāʾ because her group could not remain behind for her. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام ruled that she may depart with them and that her hajj is complete. The report addresses hardship in the rites of hajj and clarifies the practical ruling in such a constrained circumstance.
